items.title: Section: Praising Genuine Virtue — The Five Spiritual Treasures, and a Lay Scholar's Unshakeable Bows

items.zh: 又諸菩薩性好讚揚真實功德，令他歡喜。於信功德具足者前，讚揚信德令其歡喜；於戒功德具足者前，讚揚戒德令其歡喜；於聞功德具足者前，讚揚聞德令其歡喜；於捨功德具足者前，讚揚捨德令其歡喜；於慧功德具足者前，讚揚慧德令其歡喜。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, by nature, delight in praising genuine virtue, bringing others joy. Before one genuinely possessing the virtue of faith, they praise that virtue of faith, bringing joy; before one possessing discipline, they praise discipline; before one possessing learning, they praise learning; before one possessing generosity, they praise generosity; before one possessing wisdom, they praise wisdom — each bringing joy in turn.

items.title: Section: Correcting Wrongdoing — Three Grades of Reproof, and Expulsion Temporary or Lifelong

items.zh: 又諸菩薩性好悲愍，以調伏法調伏有情。若諸有情有下品過下品違犯，內懷親愛無損惱心，以軟訶責而訶責之。若諸有情有中品過中品違犯，內懷親愛無損惱心，以中訶責而訶責之。若諸有情有上品過上品違犯，內懷親愛無損惱心，以上訶責而訶責之。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, by nature moved by compassion, correct beings through fitting corrective means. Towards one with a minor fault and minor violation, holding an inwardly warm, non-harming mind, they offer gentle reproof. ... Towards one with a grave fault and grave violation, holding that same warm, non-harming mind, they offer severe reproof.

items.zh: 若諸有情有下、中品應可驅擯過失違犯，菩薩爾時為教誡彼及餘有情，以憐愍心及利益心，權時驅擯，後還攝受。若諸有情有其上品應可驅擯過失違犯，菩薩爾時盡壽驅擯，不與共住、不同受用，憐愍彼故不還攝受，
items.en: Towards one whose minor or moderate fault warrants expulsion, the bodhisattva, in order to correct both that person and others witnessing it, expels them temporarily out of compassion and genuine concern for the community's benefit, later accepting them back. Towards one whose grave fault warrants expulsion, the bodhisattva expels them for life, never dwelling or sharing resources with them again, precisely out of compassion — sparing them from accumulating even more unwholesome karma within the very community meant to help them.

items.zh: 勿令其人於佛聖教多攝非福，又為教誡利餘有情。

items.title: Section: Demonstrating Supernatural Power to Turn Beings From Evil — Nanda Shown Both Heaven and Hell

items.zh: 又諸菩薩為欲饒益諸有情故，現神通力，或為恐怖、或為引攝。謂為樂行諸惡行者，方便示現種種惡行諸果異熟。謂諸惡趣，小那落迦、大那落迦、寒那落迦、熱那落迦，既示現已，而告之言：汝當觀此，先於人中造作增長諸惡行故，今受如是最極暴惡、辛楚、非愛苦果異熟。彼見是已，恐怖厭患，離諸惡行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in order to benefit beings, display supernatural power, either to instil fear or to draw beings in. For those who delight in wrongdoing, they display the ripened fruits of such conduct — the lower realms — ... and having shown this, they say: observe this well; because of the wrongdoing accumulated and increased while human, this being now suffers this most severe, bitter, unwelcome ripened result. Seeing this, the person feels genuine fear and disgust, and abandons wrongdoing.

items.zh: 復有一類無信有情，菩薩眾中隨事故問，彼作異思拒而不答。菩薩爾時或便化作執金剛神，或復化作壯色大身巨力藥叉，令其恐怖。由是因緣，捨慢生信，恭敬正答；其餘大眾聞彼正答，亦皆調伏。

items.title: Section: Wonders That Inspire Joy, Settling Every Being in the Five Spiritual Treasures — Benefiting Beings Concludes

items.zh: 或現種種神通變化，或一為多，或多為一，或以其身穿過石壁、山巖等障往還無礙，如是廣說乃至梵世身自在轉，現無量種神變差別，或復現入火界定等，或復示現共聲聞等種種神通，方便引攝，令諸有情踊躍歡喜。諸未信者，方便安處信具足中；諸犯戒者，方便安處戒具足中；諸少聞者，方便安處聞具足中；多慳悋者，方便安處捨具足中；諸惡慧者，方便安處慧具足中。
items.en: Bodhisattvas display all manner of wondrous transformation — one body becoming many, many becoming one, passing freely through solid stone and mountain rock — ... skilfully drawing beings in, filling them with genuine joy. Those without faith are skilfully settled in the fullness of faith; those who have broken precepts, in the fullness of discipline; those who have heard little teaching, in the fullness of learning; those given to stinginess, in the fullness of generosity; and those of distorted understanding, in the fullness of wisdom.

items.zh: 如是菩薩成就一切種饒益有情戒。是名菩薩三種戒藏，亦名無量大功德藏。謂律儀戒所攝戒藏，攝善法戒所攝戒藏，饒益有情戒
items.en: In this way, bodhisattvas accomplish discipline benefiting beings in its every kind. These are called a bodhisattva's three storehouses of discipline, also called the boundless, great treasury of merit. ... Restraint discipline settles the mind; discipline gathering wholesome practice matures one's own path towards buddhahood; discipline benefiting beings matures other beings.

items.title: Section: A New Topic Opens — The Actual Ceremony of Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts

items.zh: 若諸菩薩欲於如是菩薩所學三種戒藏勤修學者，或是在家、或是出家，先於無上正等菩提發弘願已，當審訪求同法菩薩，已發大願、有智有力於語表義能授能開。
items.en: Bodhisattvas wishing to diligently train in these three storehouses of discipline, whether householder or renunciant, having first made the great vow towards unsurpassed, perfect awakening, should earnestly seek out a fellow bodhisattva who has already made that same great vow, and who has the wisdom and ability to genuinely convey and clarify its meaning.

items.zh: 於如是等功德具足勝菩薩所，先禮雙足，如是請言：我今欲於善男子所、或長老所、或大德所，乞受一切菩薩淨戒，唯願須臾不辭勞倦，哀愍聽授。
items.en: Before such a genuinely qualified bodhisattva, one first bows at their feet, and requests in these words: I now wish, good sir, elder, or venerable one, to request all the pure precepts of a bodhisattva. I ask only that you not consider this brief moment a burden, and, out of compassion, grant it to me.

items.title: Section: Reverent Offering to Every Buddha Across Every Time — One Buddha's Nature Is Every Buddha's Nature

items.zh: 既作如是無倒請已，偏袒右肩，恭敬供養十方三世諸佛世尊、已入大地得大智慧得大神力諸菩薩眾，現前專念彼諸功德，隨其所有功德因力，生殷淨心或少淨心。
items.en: Having made this genuine request, one bares the right shoulder and reverently makes offerings to the buddhas of the ten directions and three times, and to the bodhisattvas already established on the noble grounds, possessing great wisdom and great power — calling their qualities directly to mind, and, through the power of those very qualities, giving rise to a sincere and pure devotion, or, at the very least, some measure of it.

blocks.text: The last ways of benefiting beings, then the actual ceremony for receiving the bodhisattva precepts begins.

Before one who has faith, praise faith; likewise discipline, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Discipline "opens onto a favourable realm"; generosity "onto never lacking resources"; wisdom overcomes narrow views. Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a lay scholar of Yogācāra to whom monks bowed.

For a minor fault, gentle counsel "with an inwardly warm, non-harming mind"; moderate, firmer reproof; grave, punishment or expulsion, "temporary out of compassion", or for life. Master Cháng Bǎi: punishment is bodily; reproof, verbal.

To instil fear of wrongdoing, or to draw beings in. Master Cháng Bǎi tells how the Buddha showed Nanda, who missed his beautiful wife, both heaven and hell. Then "those without faith are settled in faith; precept-breakers in discipline; the unlearned in learning; the stingy in generosity; the foolish in wisdom".
"These are the three storehouses of discipline, also called the boundless, great treasury of merit."

A bodhisattva, lay or monastic, having made the great vow, goes to "a bodhisattva who shares the same teaching, has made the great vow, is wise and able to convey the precepts". Bowing at their feet: "I now wish to request all the pure precepts of a bodhisattva; please grant them to me for a short while" (Master Cháng Bǎi: a xūyú, forty-eight minutes). Then, "baring the right shoulder", one makes offerings to all Buddhas and bodhisattvas, past, present, and future.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas delight in praising genuine virtue. Which five virtues does the treatise list?
quiz.why: The treatise praises faith, discipline, learning, generosity, and wisdom in those who possess them. Master Cháng Bǎi: in the great ocean of the dharma, faith lets one enter and wisdom lets one cross.

quiz.q: When discussing praise of virtue, what story about the lay scholar Zhōu Shūjiā do the lectures tell?
options: he wrote many Yogācāra books and founded Buddhist colleges; some monastics jeered from upstairs, "Muddle-headed Zhōu is out!" yet he remained reverent
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Layman Zhōu Shūjiā wrote many books on Yogācāra; some monastics standing upstairs mocked him, "Muddle-headed Zhōu is out!" Venerable Miào Jìng tells the same story.

quiz.q: In correcting beings, how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "punishment" from "reproof"?
options: punishment is a physical, bodily penalty; reproof is only verbal
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: punishment is a physical penalty involving bodily action; reproof is merely verbal censure. Venerable Miào Jìng: "chǔ" is a cane — taking up a cane to strike.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas display supernatural power to benefit beings. What two purposes does the treatise give?
options: either to instil fear or to draw beings in
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, in order to benefit beings, display supernatural power, either to instil fear or to draw beings in." Venerable Miào Jìng: this requires supernatural power — without it, what could one do?

quiz.q: On displaying the lower realms to frighten beings away from evil, what story of Nanda does Master Cháng Bǎi tell?
options: after ordaining, Nanda kept thinking of his beautiful wife; shown the hells, he saw an empty heated iron cauldron waiting for him
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha's cousin Nanda, after ordaining, kept thinking of his beautiful wife and wanted to go home. Among the hells there was one hot iron cauldron with no one in it — waiting for him. He went back, practised the four truths diligently, and became an arhat.

quiz.q: Having drawn beings in through wonders, where are "the very stingy" skilfully settled?
quiz.why: "Those without faith are settled in the fullness of faith; precept-breakers in discipline; the unlearned in learning; the very stingy in generosity; those of poor wisdom in wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: a bodhisattva does not keep displaying powers — the aim is to lead people to the dharma.

quiz.q: The candidate asks, "I ask only that you not consider this brief moment (xūyú) a burden." How long does Master Cháng Bǎi say a xūyú is?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "I ask only that within this short xūyú (forty-eight minutes)…"
